_comment: Technical Design v0.34's In-World Names: what characters hear in place of the game's own names. Docs, code, the game record, and the system prompts (10a–10d) keep the game names. Setting content: it belongs in the setting pack with the roster, so a reskin renames these in one file. Moved here from scenarios/ with TD v0.38's Setting Pack. The names load only when both docs use them (since); a prompt never mixes the two sets.

phase._comment: Block 5's {phase_label}. A round of mingling is cut into thirds of its turns: early, midway, late.

time._comment: The short form that opens each block 6 line, in place of T4.

arrival._comment: TD v0.36: the time before the first council (in the mini-game, turn 0: the attendance notes and the opening), in place of "1st round, early". Block 5's phase label and block 6's time label.

narrator._comment: TD v0.36: the speaker code writes on the narrator's memory entries (joins, departures, withdrawals, returns, broadcasts). The same name in the game and in-world.
narrator.name: Il Notaio

acts._comment: Block 9e's act words, in-world → game act. A game word (kill, guard, investigate) is accepted too, without a repair.

retitling._comment: TD v0.50's In-World Names, Retitling (Mechanics v0.36): a French pension became a payroll payment that puts a guest on France's payroll, and a Capannello became a group. TD 0.50 loads only with Characters 0.16, the first whose briefings say "payroll", and that Characters version only with TD 0.50 or later, so the two words never meet in one prompt.

conversations._comment: The conversation words, moved out of code with TD v0.50's retitling. Keyed by the game's kind (`capannello`, `colloquio`, `gathering`). `label`: block 5's {conversation_label}, where {in_place} is notaio.json's room.in_place (" in the loggia") or empty, {others} the others joined by "and", and a Colloquio's {utterance} of {cap}. `type`: the type label that block 6's lines carry ("2nd round, early · group · …"), and `with` the label naming who else was there. From TD 0.50 these are the in-world words; `game` holds the game's own names, which a game before TD 0.50 hears in their place, and which the record, the reports, and the recorder's prompts (10a–10d) keep.
